solution: 2 — 98.6 °F is a normal body temperature (37 °C); 98.6 °C would be close to boiling water (100 °C) and no one could survive it. A real doctor would never mix up the units. (Normal adult resting pulse 60–100 bpm; 120/80 mmHg is a normal blood pressure.)
